newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: CRICKET-CRONJE SPARES SOUTH AFRICA'S BLUSHES.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-CRONJE SPARES SOUTH AFRICA'S BLUSHES.

text.p: A captain's innings from Hansie Cronje spared South Africa's blushes as they beat Zimbabwe by five wickets in the triangular day/night match at Centurion Park on Saturday.

After Zimbabwe had under-achieved in being bowled out for 211 on a good pitch, South Africa collapsed to seven for three and 43 for four before Cronje arrived to shepherd his team to victory with 23 balls to spare at 212 for five.
He put on 123 for the fifth wicket with Daryll Cullinan and was still there at the end, having scored 87 from 128 balls with five fours and a six.
Eddo Brandes, who took a hat-trick against England in a limited overs match earlier this month, got Zimbabwe off to a dream start by trapping Andrew Hudson lbw with the first ball of the innings.
Medium pacer John Rennie then plunged South Africa into crisis by taking two wickets in his first over, the second of the innings.
Lance Klusener was bowled by the first ball of Rennie's over and prolific opening batsman Gary Kirsten was caught off the last.
Heath Streak became the third bowler to take a wicket with his first ball when he had Jonty Rhodes brilliantly caught by Grant Flower in the gully for 16 to reduce South Africa to 43 for four.

With Zimbabwe on top, Cronje and Cullinan had to fight hard for runs. But they eventually gained the upperhand and when Cullinan fell in the 40th over for a fine 73 off 108 balls with three fours the job was all but done.
Earlier, opener Grant Flower held Zimbabwe's innings together, making 90 from 126 balls with eight fours before being seventh out, one of Allan Donald's four victims.
All-rounder Paul Strang made a plucky 39 from 41 balls to ensure Zimbabwe a competitive total but despite heroics by the bowlers it was never enough once Cronje got the bit between his teeth.
The next match in the series is between Zimbabwe and India in Paarl on Monday.
